strategy.thesis: One of Octopus Ventures' eight named specialist sectors is Health (alongside a separate Biotech sector); the health team backs companies at, in the firm's own words, 'the most ambitious frontiers of medical science,' spanning diagnostics, mental health, women's health and digital-care-delivery models.

backing.notes: Octopus Ventures is the venture capital arm within the wider Octopus Group (a UK financial-services group also running Octopus Energy and Octopus Investments); Wikipedia describes Octopus Ventures itself as 'a venture capital fund with assets of £1.7bn as of 2022' (i.e. external-LP-style fund economics), but the precise capital-flow relationship to Octopus Group was not resolved by sources fetched this session, so no backer row is asserted.

summary.en: London VC (£1.7bn AUM) with a formally named Health sector team (alongside a separate Biotech sector) led by Kamran Adle and Will Gibbs, backing an 11-company-plus portfolio spanning diagnostics, mental health, women's health and digital care delivery.

strategy.thesis: Internal technology-transfer and spinout-creation arm of University College London; not sector-exclusive to health, but its named flagship spinouts skew heavily medical (cell & gene therapy, oncology surgical devices, neurodegenerative disease).

summary.en: UCL's own technology-transfer and venture-creation office (UCLB, trading as UCL Ventures) — 198 spinouts since 1993 and £4.5bn in spinout capital raised since 2016, including cancer cell-therapy company Autolus Therapeutics (IPO'd) and surgical-guidance medtech Endomag.

strategy.thesis: Early-stage Nordic VC investing across two named theses — life sciences and technology/energy/sustainability — with life sciences targeting unmet medical needs where, in the firm's words, 'competence and capital are decisive when turning a laboratory result into an effective treatment.'

summary.en: Bergen-based early-stage Nordic VC (~NOK 1.3bn across 3 funds, 24 portfolio companies) investing on two theses, life sciences and cleantech, with a life-sciences portfolio including diagnostics company SonoClear and biotechs Calluna Pharma and Pluvia Biotech.
